entries.text_en: — He says: what has made him disbelieve! This verse was revealed about ʿUtba ibn Abī Lahab ibn ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib [299b — sic, for 229b]. That is because he had been angry at his father and came to Muḥammad ﷺ and believed in him; «then when his father was pleased with him and reconciled with him» [2], and equipped him and sent him off to Syria with trade goods, «he said» [3]: Convey to Muḥammad from ʿUtba that he has disbelieved in the Star (al-najm). When the Prophet ﷺ heard of that, he said: O God, set upon him Your dog to eat him. So he stopped one night on some stretch of the road, and the lion came and ate him. Then He said, while knowing: «From what thing did He create him?» (18)

surahMaterial.text_en: [Sūrat ʿAbasa (80): verses 1 to 42] In the name of God, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. He frowned and turned away (1) because the blind man came to him (2) And what would make you know — perhaps he might purify himself (3) or be reminded, and the reminder would benefit him (4) As for he who considers himself self-sufficient (5) to him you give attention (6) And it is not upon you if he does not purify himself (7) But as for he who came to you striving (8) while he fears [God] (9) from him you are distracted (10) No! Indeed, it is a reminder (11) So whoever wills may remember it (12) [It is] in honoured scrolls (13) exalted and purified (14) in the hands of scribes (safara) (15) noble and dutiful (16) May man be destroyed; how ungrateful he is! (17) From what thing did He create him? (18) From a sperm-drop He created him and determined him (19) Then He eased the way for him (20) Then He caused him to die and put him in a grave (21) Then when He wills, He will resurrect him (22) No! surahMaterial.foot_note_en:
1. The main purpose of the sūra: explaining the state of the blind man; the mention of the nobility of the Qur'an; the complaint against Abū Jahl and his denial of the resurrection and the Standing; the establishment of proof for the resurrection from the state of [text: «al-thabāt», probably «al-nabāt», «plant growth»], and the giving of life to the dead; the preoccupation of creatures in the plains [of the Gathering]; and the disparity in the states of the people of the [high] degrees and the [low] depths, in His saying: «Faces, that Day, will be bright, laughing, rejoicing at good news. And faces, that Day, will have dust upon them; darkness will cover them. Those are the disbelievers, the wicked» (Sūrat ʿAbasa: 38–42).
2. In A: «ithnān» («two»); the correct is: «ithnatān» or «thintān».
3. In the muṣḥaf: (80) Sūrat ʿAbasa, Meccan, its verses 43; revealed after Sūrat al-Najm. [.....] [Translator's note: the main text says forty-two, whereas this footnote says forty-three.]

surahMaterial.text_en: — He says: he frowned with his face and turned away to someone else. It was revealed about ʿAbd Allāh ibn Abī Sarḥ, the blind man — whose mother was Umm Maktūm; his name was ʿAmr ibn Qabs [sic, for Qays] ibn Zāʾida ibn Rawāḥa ibn al-Aṣamm ibn Ḥajar ibn ʿAbdūd ibn Bughayḍ ibn ʿĀmir ibn Luʾayy ibn Ghālib. As for Umm Maktūm, her name was ʿĀtika bint ʿĀmir ibn ʿAtika ibn ʿĀmir ibn Makhzūm ibn «Yaqaẓa» [1] ibn Murra ibn Kaʿb ibn Luʾayy. That is because one day he was sitting in the Sacred Mosque alone, with no «second» [2] person with him, and he was «a man» [3] blind of sight, when two angels descended from heaven to pray in the Sacred Mosque, and said: Who is this blind man who does not see in this world nor in the Hereafter? One of them said: But I am amazed at Abū Ṭālib, calling people to Islam! — while he does not see the two of them, but he heard that. So ʿAbd Allāh got up until he came to the Messenger of God ﷺ, and with him were Umayya ibn Khalaf [229a] and al-ʿAbbās ibn ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib, standing before him as he presented Islam to them. ʿAbd Allāh said: O Muḥammad, I have come to you repenting; is there repentance for me?
